checks.name: example: General Session opens with 5 presets, 3 destinations, 2 AUX outputs
save / load: the show is identical after a save and a reload
undo / redo: a layer change undoes and redoes
Simple: one preset tile per preset and layer chips on the canvas
Simple: Add Preset adds one, Delete removes it
Simple: copy a preset and paste it onto another
Simple: Add Destination opens its window, adds the destination, and it can be removed
Simple: Add AUX adds an output that is on in every preset, Remove takes it away
Simple: an AUX can be switched off for one preset only
Simple: the layer panel lists Position, Size, Opacity, Mask, Border, Shadow, Effects
Simple: the layer panel title reads in full and no caption in the panel is cut off
Simple: typing a Width in the layer panel resizes the layer and the height follows the lock
Simple: an Area of Interest can be switched on and off for a destination
Advanced: opens on a preset with the sources rail and the properties panel
Advanced: both side panels collapse to a strip and come back
Advanced: picking a plain layer shows Source, General, Position, Size, Opacity, Mask, Border, Shadow, Effects
Advanced: a 4:3 picture dropped on a locked layer reshapes the window to 4:3
Advanced: a media layer adds Filters, Color and Source crop sections
Advanced: Filters offers B&W, Negative and Sepia
Advanced: Width and Scale are one window (Width 960 gives Height 720 and Scale 120%)
Advanced: unlocking the aspect switches the layer to Stretch, locking again snaps it back
Advanced: a source crop reshapes a locked window, Full picture restores it
Advanced: dragging a corner of a locked layer keeps its shape and the panel follows
Advanced: a clip dropped on the BG selects the BG and lists it like a layer
Advanced: Speed is a menu of fixed steps (0, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0), a pick sets the clip rate, 0 holds a still frame
Advanced: the timeline shows transport for a picked clip and Play lights a transport key
Advanced: nothing is left playing after Pause
exports: a clip BG is written as a layer with its details
Advanced: clearing the BG source removes its picture too
Advanced: closes cleanly
Wire Simple: the diagram draws one switcher row per source and one card per source
Wire Simple: the switcher columns read # Source ID # Destination ID
Wire: renaming a source from its card reaches every preset, the I/O list and the diagram
Wire: a duplicate source name is refused
Wire: pinch (ctrl + wheel) zooms about the cursor, a plain wheel does not zoom
Wire: the All Sources header stays pinned while the cards scroll
Wire: both side panels collapse to a strip and come back
Wire: the Export window offers sheet sizes from Letter to ANSI E
Wire Advanced: page 1 is built from the show, every source wired into the switcher
Wire Advanced: switcher cells read the machine in Source and leave ID blank for a single output
Wire Advanced: a named output point shows in the ID cell, an unnamed extra point reads OUT 2
Wire Advanced: + In adds a row, × removes a free row, × on a wired row is refused
Wire Advanced: the pencil reopens the size window with the current counts, shrinking below a cable is refused
Wire Advanced: a router draws the matrix panel with numbered In and Out keys
Wire Advanced: pressing an output arms it (it blinks), pressing an input routes it, and the name follows through to the switcher
Wire Advanced: one input can feed two outputs, and an output only ever has one input
Wire Advanced: a converter and a network switch can be added and grow a port
Wire Advanced: a tile that grows pushes the tile stacked under it down by the same amount
Wire Advanced: a new router or switcher never lands on another tile
Wire Advanced: a page can be copied and the copy closed
Wire: closes cleanly
